items.title: Paper Trail
items.intent: Ch1 story mission. Collect five loose ledger slips blowing around Saltmouth (collect x5 across saltmouth anchors). Teaches the town layout. Ends with Tamsin noticing a ledger page filled in by no living hand. Rewards credits + rep.guild + flag ch1-paper-trail.done.

items.title: Debt Shield
items.intent: Ch1 story mission. Ketch sends Ash to pick up second-hand gyro parts from the reclaimer trader camped at saltmouth:gate-east and deliver them to the garage — the first upgrade discount. Teaches the garage. Flags ch1-debt-shield.done; unlocks garage tip dialogue.

items.title: A Fair Price for Water
items.intent: Ch1 story mission (timed). Rush a cracked condenser coil from the Guild exchange to the water tower before the afternoon window. timeLimit ~150s. Introduces timers without stakes. Flags ch1-watering.done.

items.title: The Hum
items.intent: Ch1 story finale. Follow the crate's fading signal: goto three beacons (saltmouth:flats-pan, saltmouth:overlook, saltmouth:gate-east). Radio beats with Tamsin/Ketch escalate; final beat: Ash's name appears in the ledger by itself. Flags ch1-the-hum.done + lore:driftline-creed.

items.title: The Guild's Offer
items.intent: Ch2 story. Deliver the null-crate custody papers to skydocks:dockmaster on the mesa — the Guild wants the crate archived. Sets faction offers in motion. Requires ch1-the-hum.done. Dialogue choice: promise the Guild preference (flag offer.guild) or hedge.

items.title: The Choir's Offer
items.intent: Ch2 story. Deliver a listening crystal to choirhollow:listening-horn; Cantor Ilex hears the crate's hum through it. Alternative path to ch2-guild-offer; flags offer.choir. Gentle, eerie dialogue.

items.title: The Reclaimers' Offer
items.intent: Ch2 story. Haul a crate of 'definitely legal' cutting charges to cinderflats:crusher for Aunt Vertex; Boss Pyke offers to open the null crate. Flags offer.reclaimers. Humor-heavy.

items.title: Run the Glassroad
items.intent: Ch2 story (race). A timed checkpoint race down the glassroad canyon (gate-south → slick-mile → mid-span → glass-chapel → gate-north). Slick grip teaches braking. Jett Marrows taunts on the radio. Flags ch2-glassroad-race.done + rep driftline cred.

items.title: Lamp Convoy
items.intent: Ch2 story (escort). Escort the Choir's lamp relighting procession between lamp ring anchors at choirhollow; keep pace inside a moving radius, lose stragglers if you outrun them. Flags ch2-lamp-convoy.done.

items.title: First Word
items.intent: Ch2 finale (scout). Hit three high viewpoints (windspine:ridge-crest, skydocks:mesa-top, glassroad:glass-chapel) tuning the radio; on the third, MOTHER speaks one word: 'ASH.' Flags ch2-first-word.done, mother.speaks, lore:mother-primer.

items.title: The First Wall
items.intent: Ch3 opener (storm). A wall of sand swallows windspine: outrun it from windspine:storm-gauge to saltmouth:gate-east with the storm front chasing (storm type). Introduces storm mechanics. Flags ch3-first-wall.done.

items.title: Courier Down
items.intent: Ch3 story. Rill Davenant's beacon went dark mid-run. Collect 4 transponder fragments scattered around windspine. Ketch's radio goes uncharacteristically quiet. Sets rill.missing.

items.title: Into the Wall
items.intent: Ch3 story (storm). Deliberately ride INTO a moving storm front to reach Rill's dropped cache between the ridge and flats. Visibility gameplay (fog spike). Flags rill.cache.

items.title: Static Litany
items.intent: Ch3 story (fragile + timed). Deliver unbroken choir-glass to choirhollow through a storm window; Static-Warden Pem reads storm noise from your cargo. Damage penalty mechanics shine. Flags ch3-static-litany.done.

items.title: Salvage Rights
items.intent: Ch3 story. Reclaimers vs Guild dispute over a stranded crawler; courier arbitration: deliver both claim tokens between cinderflats and skydocks and pick who signs first (choice flag salvage.guild / salvage.reclaimers).

items.title: The Shelter Line
items.intent: Ch3 finale (escort). Find Rill half-mad in an erosion cave, escort him home slow and safe; he recites coordinates in his sleep. Sets rill.found + rill.coordinates; radio beat: the coordinates glow on Ash's map.

items.title: Coordinates
items.intent: Ch4 opener (scout). Rill's sleep-talk coordinates lead to three old survey pylons (mothersgate:approach region). Plot them; they triangulate the Door. Requires rill.found.

items.title: The Key
items.intent: Ch4 story (fragile). Recover the null crate from the south-gate relay cache and carry it — humming loud now — to mothersgate:approach. Sprint pacing, storm flanks. Flags crate.at-gate.

items.title: Three Fires
items.intent: Ch4 story. Visit all three faction leaders (skydocks, choirhollow, cinderflats) — each makes their final case for the gate combination. Dialogue choice sets gate.ally (guild|choir|reclaimers|none).

items.title: Glass Blooms
items.intent: Ch4 story. The desert begins to change: glass blossoms erupt along the glassroad. Collect 5 bloom samples for the Choir while the canyon's grip and colours shift. World-state flags start region visual changes. Flags ch4-blooms.done.

items.title: The Door Opens Like a Flower
items.intent: Ch4 finale (goto → dialogue setpiece). Bring the crate to mothersgate:the-door; it opens petal by petal. Long scripted dialogue with MOTHER's first full sentences. Sets gate.open + lore:mother-voice.

items.title: Last Deliveries
items.intent: Ch5 opener. Three farewell drops in one run — Ketch's tea, Pemmy's oats, a letter Tamsin never sends. Quiet, warm, deliberately slow before the storm. Unlocks after gate.open.

items.title: The Choice-Core
items.intent: Ch5 story (fragile). MOTHER hands over her choice-core — her waking, held in your hands. Carry it out of the cradle to the rally point; every faction offers escort and arguments.

items.title: Storm of Storms
items.intent: Ch5 story (storm). The biggest storm on record closes every route; thread canyons and ridge lines from choirhollow to mothersgate against three chasing fronts. Peak mechanics test.

items.title: The Skyship Ballot
items.intent: Ch5 story (race/timed). The settlements vote on Kessa-9's future by skyship beacon relay; you're the relay. Checkpoint route linking windspine → skydocks → saltmouth under a hard time limit.

items.title: Last Delivery
items.intent: Ch5 finale (deliver + choice). One final run to the Door carrying the choice-core through whatever the desert has left. At the threshold a dialogue choice: wake MOTHER (flag ending.rain — credit crawl over blooming desert) or return her to sleep (flag ending.quiet — credits over the unchanged hard free land). Both endings fully staged.

items.title: Dune Mail Express
items.intent: Side (deliver). Three-drop mail run linking saltmouth outskirts beacons in a loop; generous pay, no clock. Board staple.

items.title: Choir Glassware
items.intent: Side (fragile). Carry singing-glass windchimes from choirhollow:lamp-ring to skydocks:keel-town. High payout scaled by remaining integrity; shield upgrades matter.

items.title: Against the Condenser
items.intent: Side (timed). Water credits expire at dusk: exchange → water tower → moorage in 120s. Teaches town shortcuts; repeatable-feel board filler.

items.title: A Pocketful of Spark Plugs
items.intent: Side (collect). Solder lost six ignition plugs along the yard fence; sweep cinderflats anchors collecting them. Reclaimers rep.

items.title: Turbine Audit
items.intent: Side (collect). Windspine survey camp needs 4 birds'-nest debris cleared from turbine anchors. Light platforming hops.

items.title: Crests and Cairns
items.intent: Side (scout). Photograph-equivalent: visit three high viewpoints (overlook, crater-rim, ridge-crest). Teaches landmarks for later chapters.

items.title: Rematch: Jett Marrows
items.intent: Side (race). Jett challenges you on a salt-flat circuit (3 laps of 4 gates around saltmouth). Taunting radio. Pays well.

items.title: Rematch: The Quicklime Kid
items.intent: Side (race). The Quicklime Kid rides dirt circles around the drowned-array pan; technical slalom gates between sunken panels.

items.title: Lost: One (1) Crate, Rustic
items.intent: Side (collect→deliver). A Reclaimer crate bounced off a hauler somewhere on the saltmouth→drowned road; find 3 impact marks, then deliver the crate to the array cairn.

items.title: Lost: The Usual Crate
items.intent: Side (collect). Same joke, worse outcome: the crate split open. Collect 5 packets of 'agricultural material' (definitely seeds) around choirhollow before the Choir notices/absconds.

items.title: Keel Town Quarterly
items.intent: Side (deliver). Mail bag up the winch to skydocks:keel-town and back down the long way for landing practice. First time many players climb the mesa.

items.title: Night Supply Window
items.intent: Side (timed). The storm gauge crew only opens their hatch at night; deliver battery cells saltmouth→windspine:storm-gauge after dark. Teaches day/night awareness.

items.title: Relay Repair Round
items.intent: Side (collect). The Driftline's radio relays need new horizon cells: collect 3 battery drops at flats-pan, gate-east and overlook, then goto the mast at moorage to re-sync.

items.title: Canyon Post
items.intent: Side (deliver). The mid-span shrine keeper orders books. Yes, books. Deliver a shockproof satchel to glassroad:mid-span without cracking the spines (fragile-lite).

items.title: The Weather Goat's Window
items.intent: Side (timed, storm-lite). Pemmy the Guild weather goat predicts a 3-minute clear window; deliver sensor wax to the storm gauge and return before the wall closes. Comic timing mission.

items.title: Beacon Sweep
items.intent: Side (scout). Driftline obligation: re-light 4 road beacons between saltmouth and glassroad gate-south. Pays little, counts much (driftline flavour).

items.title: Feed the Crusher
items.intent: Side (collect). Aunt Vertex pays by the bucket for glass shards blown off the canyon rim; collect 6 at glassroad rim anchors. Danger-adjacent.

items.title: Letters for the Drowned
items.intent: Side (deliver). The array substation's automated caretaker still answers mail. Deliver 2 bundles to drowned-array:substation; melancholy sci-fi beat.

items.title: Crest Dash
items.intent: Side (race). Pure speed trial: survey-camp → ridge-crest → south-foot gates with a hard time. Windspine's signature sprint.

items.title: The Mesa Perch
items.intent: Side (scout). Visit skydocks:mesa-top and dockmaster at golden hour for the Guild's photo survey of 'approachability'. Max views, minimal risk.

items.title: The Salt Tax
items.intent: Side (deliver, fragile). Sister Counterweight audits the salt piles; carry her impossibly delicate calibration weights Saltmouth loop. Satire of bureaucracy, brutal integrity math.

items.title: Hollow Chimes
items.intent: Side (collect). Little Reverb heard chimes where no lamps burn; collect 4 resonance pebbles around choirhollow rim at night. Eerie-cute.

items.title: The Long Way Home
items.intent: Side (deliver). An old moorage hand pays you to 'lose' his eviction notice — deliver it to the wrong dock, then back to the exchange with apologies. Warm humor, double-leg route.

items.title: Static for the Choir
items.intent: Side (collect). Pem wants storm static recordings: hold position near 3 charged glass spires in the canyon until the meter fills (goto with dwell).

items.title: Guild Runner: Contracts
items.intent: Side (timed). Three Guild contracts, three towns, one afternoon: exchange → dockmaster → boss-office and back. Route-planning exam.

items.title: Ember Run
items.intent: Side (deliver, night). Reclaimers pay double for a warm reactor brick cinderflats→choirhollow before it cools (decay timer). Visual: glowing cargo light on the bike.

items.title: A Favour of Paint
items.intent: Side (deliver). Ketch wants rare ochre pigment from the drowned-array cache; reward is a free paint unlock + garage banter.

items.title: Messages for Nobody
items.intent: Side (deliver). The substation caretaker's outbound queue: deliver 3 old messages whose recipients are gone; Ketch reads them anyway. Quiet worldbuilding payoff.

items.title: A Following Wind
items.intent: Side (race). Fun run with Ketch riding shotgun-commentary over the radio: salt flats grand loop, 5 gates. Pure joy baseline mission.

items.title: Interest Payment
items.intent: Side (collect). The Guild offers debt relief for recovering 6 scattered invoice tags blown off the exchange roof across town. Debt mechanic tie-in.

items.title: Old Roads
items.intent: Ch5 story (scout). Before the final choice, MOTHER asks to see the world she half-made: ride the original terraform survey route (5 overlooks across all regions). She comments on each in radio static-glimpses. Sets up the ending's emotional weight.

items.title: Brinemaster Ogo
items.intent: Guildmaster of the Salt Guild, skydocks. Huge patient man who chairs disputes like weather. Wants the crate archived before it 'makes history — history is bad for margins'. 8+ lines incl. radio.

items.title: Sister Counterweight
items.intent: Guild auditor-titular who weighs salt and souls on the same brass scale. Speaks in inventory metaphors. Was forever changed by weighing the null crate. Comic-ominous.

items.title: Factor Marn Phlox
items.intent: Junior Guild factor at the glassroad south gate relay post; perpetually underqualified, cheerful, terrified of the canyon. Relay contact for ch1-null-crate.

items.title: Dockmaster Devanna Shore
items.intent: Runs the skydocks mesa; ex-skyship captain, measures everything in knots and grudges. Handles ch2 guild-offer delivery.

items.title: Cantor Ilex
items.intent: Voice of the Choir at choirhollow. Gentle, unnerving, genuinely kind; hears the crate through walls. Speaks of MOTHER as 'she who fell asleep mid-sentence'. Central ch2-choir-offer.

items.title: Static-Warden Pem
items.intent: Choir's listener-in-chief; carries a dead radio that isn't dead. Translates static litanies. About 30% oracle, 70% antenna.

items.title: Little Reverb
items.intent: Nine-year-old Choir kid who hears MOTHER clearest of anyone and is completely unimpressed by it. Collects 'echoes' (side content). Disarms every tense scene.

items.title: Brother Decibel
items.intent: Choir's sound-keeper; talks too loud because he listens too hard. Maintains the listening horns. Comic volume-control problem.

items.title: Boss Pyke
items.intent: Reclaimer yard boss at cinderflats. Hands like vices, ledger like a poem. Wants the crate opened 'carefully, with the biggest drill'. Central ch2-reclaimer-offer.

items.title: Solder
items.intent: Young reclaimer mechanic who idolizes the Wren ('she's held together with spite, I love her'). Side-mission giver for parts; nervy crush energy aimed at the bike, mostly.

items.title: Aunt Vertex
items.intent: Reclaimer explosives theologian. Believes demolition is a conversation with structure. Pays for glass shards; laughs like gravel in a bucket.

items.title: Compass
items.intent: Reclaimer pathfinder who maps which ruins are 'load-bearing historically'. Dry cartographer humor; gives route tips as radio chatter.

items.title: Rill Davenant
items.intent: Senior Driftline courier who vanishes in ch3. Warm show-off; owes Ketch money he insists is 'an investment'. Found half-mad reciting coordinates; his rescue arc is the heart of ch3.

items.title: Jett Marrows
items.intent: Rival courier, salt-flat circuit. Impeccable leathers, insufferable wink, secretly cheers Ash in ch5. Race missions + radio taunts.

items.title: The Quicklime Kid
items.intent: Masked rival at the drowned array; communicates in engine revs and one-word radio messages. Nobody knows their deal; everyone enjoys the mystery.

items.title: Madame Traction
items.intent: Independent fixer in Keel Town (skydocks); sells rumours and grip tape. Knows about the ledger-entry that wrote itself before Ash does. Noir-ish connector.

items.title: Old Bahro
items.intent: Retired miner at the moorage mast who claims he helped pour the glassroad. Tells contradictory stories; all of them partly true.

items.title: Salt Singer Ila
items.intent: Busker who plays the salt flats' resonance with a bowed rail; gives weather hints in verse. Ambient character; her songs telegraph storms.

items.title: Dusk-Farmer Ook
items.intent: Grows lichen in the shadow of the boundary mountains; trades in 'things that grow where nothing should'. Quest-giver for ember-run style night jobs.

items.title: Ferry-Pilot Wisp
items.intent: Skyship ferry pilot between skydocks and the flats; chronically early, cosmically calm. Gives aerial gossip on the radio.

items.title: Pemmy (Weather Goat)
items.intent: The Guild weather desk is a goat. Pemmy's bleats are translated by factors with a straight face. Her predictions are alarmingly accurate. Yes she gets 8 lines. Yes they're all bleats with subtitles.

items.title: MOTHER
items.intent: The dormant terraforming AI waking by degrees. Voice = kind librarian groping out of deep sleep; misunderstandings are enormous and gentle. ch2 first word through ch5 full dialogue. Lines must serve radio (short, staticky) and finale.

items.title: Shrine-Keeper Toll
items.intent: Lone keeper of the glassroad mid-span shrine. Orders books. Reads them aloud to the canyon so the echo 'finishes the sentences'. Quiet melancholy host character.

items.title: Surveyor Kest
items.intent: Windspine survey-camp lead; all blunt edges and meteorology. Storm-mission technical voice; secretly writes terrible love poems about isobars.

items.title: Marshal Dune
items.intent: Self-appointed (and only) law of the cinderflats approaches; has a badge made from a hubcap and the moral authority of a tired parent. Keeps Reclaimers and Guild honest-ish.

items.title: The Evening Standard
items.intent: Radio host of the nightly broadcast heard between regions; dry headlines of your own deeds a day late and slightly wrong. A chorus character — radio-heavy line set.

items.title: Nona Vex
items.intent: Skydocks fuel mistress; converts skyships to寺院 no— converts skycranes to run on stormstatic. Sells boost-cell upgrades with minimal eye contact.

items.title: Caretaker Unit 7
items.intent: The drowned array's automated caretaker that still answers mail and requests. Battered speaker mast voice; politeness as programming and as tragedy. Side content heart-string puller.

items.title: Hollis Fenn
items.intent: Skydocks dockmaster, home skydocks. Runs Keel Town's moorage with a ship's-bell voice and smuggler's discretion. Guild-adjacent but fond of couriers. Needed for ch2-guild-offer completion beats and side-sky-mail.

items.title: Warden of the Span
items.intent: Keeper of the glassroad:mid-span shrine, home glassroad. A hermit who orders books by courier and annotates the margins of reality. Slow, funny, sad. Needed for side-canyon-post.

items.title: Caretaker Unit SEVEN
items.intent: The Drowned Array's automated caretaker, home drowned-array. A failing pre-collapse machine that still answers its mail. Polite error messages as personality; quietly heartbreaking. Needed for side-pan-letters and side-theo-messages.

items.title: Mags Delver
items.intent: Reclaimer hauler and poet (yes), home cinderflats. Writes odes to machines she strips. Source of salvage gossip and gentle humour; mentioned in side-lost-crate-1.

items.title: Windspine Ridge: Field Guide Appendix
items.intent: Field-guide entry, 250+ words: turbine lumber no— turbine lore, ridge etiquette, storm-gauge duties, why surveyors tap the towers before dawn.

items.title: The Glassroad: Advanced Appendix
items.intent: Field-guide, 250+ words: grip physics of fused glass, vein heat, drift lines, the mid-span shrine, the legend of the first courier to drift the Slick Mile.

items.title: The Skydocks: Mooring Manual (Public Extract)
items.intent: Field-guide, 250+ words: mesa winds, winch etiquette, skyship classes, why Keel Town hangs off the west rim specifically.

items.title: The Cinderflats: What's Still Hot
items.intent: Field-guide, 250+ words: Reclaimer safety aphorisms, the Crusher, sorted-pile categories, which alarms matter and which are 'just opinions'.

items.title: Choir Hollow: A Visitor's Manners
items.intent: Field-guide, 250+ words: lamp ring etiquette, why you don't take radios past the steps, listening-horn hours, how to politely decline a static litany.

items.title: The Drowned Array: Reading the Cairns
items.intent: Field-guide, 250+ words: courier cache code in stone cairns, panel-field shortcuts, the caretaker's mail round, why the pan shines at dusk.

items.title: The Boundary Mountains: File You Under Weather
items.intent: Field-guide, 250+ words: why no one crosses the violet rim, the three documented attempts, what the air does to radios up there.

items.title: Terraforming Kessa-9: The Prospectus (Annotated)
items.intent: Machine record, 250+ words: the original corporate pitch for Kessa-9's terraforming, with bitter margin notes from later settlers. 'Phase 3: Rains' never shipped.

items.title: The Delay: An Oral History
items.intent: Log/oral history, 250+ words: five voices on the day the money ran out — a treasurer, a teacher, a terraforming tech, a child, and the person who pulled the plug.

items.title: MOTHER: Boot Sequence, Partial Log
items.intent: Machine record, 250+ words: fragmentary boot log from the dormant terraforming AI — checksum errors that read like yawns; the last line timestamps tomorrow.

items.title: Things I Meant to Finish (MOTHER, draft 0)
items.intent: Machine record, 250+ words: the AI's half-written design memoir — poems about aquifers, strong opinions on dune spacing, one paragraph that is clearly an apology.

items.title: MOTHER's Voice: Transcript of First Sentence
items.intent: Machine record, 250+ words: the Chorus-transcribed first full sentence spoken in ch4, with competing marginalia from Guild, Choir and Reclaimer readers. Unlock flag lore:mother-voice.

items.title: Static Litany I: The Sleeping Garden
items.intent: Choir tract, 250+ words: the foundational litany — MOTHER as gardener asleep mid-sentence; the rain that was promised; a lullaby structure with liturgical jokes.

items.title: Static Litany IX: The Courier's Part
items.intent: Choir tract, 250+ words: a litany about couriers as 'the walking stamens'; the Driftline resents being scripture but the pay metaphor is decent.

items.title: Minutes of the Hollow Disputation
items.intent: Choir log, 250+ words: meeting minutes politely recording a theological schism about whether the null crate's hum is in a major key (it is a cappella heresy).

items.title: Ledger Excerpts: Year One of the Delay
items.intent: Guild tract, 250+ words: the first year's ledger — ration arithmetic, the birth of the board system, one entry for 'hope, misc., quantity: sufficient'.

items.title: A Complete History of Form 22-B
items.intent: Guild tract, 250+ words: the anomalous-cargo form's 214-year evolution, including the intralking— including the incident with the bees, the ghost net, and the crate that filed itself.

items.title: On Debt: A Guild Doctrine Pamphlet
items.intent: Guild tract, 250+ words: why the Guild holds debts, why it forgives them at a hundred years, and the famous footnote about Ash Varga-style 'ambition balances'.

items.title: The Reclaimer Field Manual (7th Edition, Burnt)
items.intent: Reclaimer tract, 250+ words: extraction rules, the Load-Bearing Historically doctrine, how to retire a turbine politely, Aunt Vertex's foreword ('things fall down, that's physics being honest').

items.title: Sparks: A Reclaimer Work Song
items.intent: Reclaimer tract, 250+ words: call-and-response work song for coordinated pulls, with verse annotations about famous salvage jobs and one verse everyone refuses to explain.

items.title: The Crusher: Service Record
items.intent: Machine record, 250+ words: the maintenance log of the Yards' beloved crusher — 40 years of 'still operational' entries, each more affectionate than the last.

items.title: The Driftline Creed (With Commentary)
items.intent: Driftline tract, 250+ words: 'Any crate, any storm, any door' — origins, exceptions, the footnote about the crate that hums. Unlock flag lore:driftline-creed.

items.title: Courier Slang: A Field Lexicon
items.intent: Driftline log, 250+ words: flat-salt, following wind, knot-happy, glass-sick, hummer (crates that hum), and forty more terms with example sentences.

items.title: Rill Davenant's Flight Log — Early Entries
items.intent: Personal log, 250+ words: young Rill learning the flats; jokes that stop being jokes when you know what's coming in ch3.

items.title: Rill Davenant's Flight Log — The Gap
items.intent: Personal log, 250+ words: entries before the vanishing; route to the survey pylons annotated with 'if you're reading this, wrong, but keep reading'.

items.title: The Coordinates (Transcribed From Sleep)
items.intent: Personal log, 250+ words: Ketch's bedside transcription of everything Rill recited in his sleep; half numbers, half lullaby; one parenthetical that MOTHER interrupts to correct.

items.title: Evening Standard: Storm Season Special (Transcript)
items.intent: Broadcast, 250+ words: the nightly radio's storm season kickoff — safety tips, goat forecast drama, and one story that is clearly about Ash with the name mispronounced.

items.title: Evening Standard: The Salvage-Rights Summit (Transcript)
items.intent: Broadcast, 250+ words: coverage of the Guild-Reclaimer dispute the player arbitrate in ch3, with post-match punditry and a weather goat exclusive.

items.title: Evening Standard: The Night the Desert Changed
items.intent: Broadcast, 250+ words: the finale broadcast — either the night of first rain or the night of chosen quiet, written to serve both endings with one unreconciled sentence each way.

items.title: Know Your Skyship: A Spotter's Card
items.intent: Record/poster, 250+ words: envelopes, gondolas, moorage classes, famous hulls (the Bureaucratic Reminder, the Following Wind), and spotting etiquette.

items.title: Water Rights and Other Wells
items.intent: Guild tract, 250+ words: condenser law, tower shifts, the concept of 'fair price', and why the moorage crew pays in stories.

items.title: Saltflat Cuisine: Recipes of the Delay
items.intent: Log/recipes, 250+ words: salt-baked lichen, storm bread (baked by static), the Guild's ceremonial 'counted stew'. Warm and funny.

items.title: Your Hover-Bike and You
items.intent: Field-guide, 250+ words: horizon cells, gyro cages, boost cells, cargo shields — a courier's maintenance primer as flat prose.

items.title: The First Courier (Probably)
items.intent: Log/legend, 250+ words: the founding myth of the Driftline — one rider, one crate, one closing storm, and a door that opened. Sister cities dispute every detail.

items.title: The Long Audit: Sister Counterweight's Memoir
items.intent: Log, 250+ words: excerpts from the auditor's private record — the night she weighed the null crate, and why she now counts backwards.

items.title: The Goat Forecast: Methodology (Contested)
items.intent: Record/comedy, 250+ words: the Guild weather desk's official defense of Pemmy's methods, with appendices by three scientists and one brave child.

items.title: Botanical Emergency Bulletin 4: Glass Blooms
items.intent: Record, 250+ words: first official notice of the ch4 glass blooms — four parties' annotations creep steadily from alarm toward wonder.

items.title: Survey of the Sealed Cradle (Abandoned)
items.intent: Machine record, 250+ words: the original corporate survey of mothersgate, abandoned mid-form; the form keeps trying to complete itself across the document.

items.title: Hymns for a Door
items.intent: Choir tract, 250+ words: verses the Choir keeps by the cradle door, in several meters, one of which is secretly a materials-fatigue manual.

items.title: Accounts of Rain (Pre-Delay)
items.intent: Oral history, 250+ words: what rain was, from people who remember it — smell, noise, invoices for umbrellas, one person who hated it and is now mythologically wrong.

items.title: The Choice Warrant (Template, Unused)
items.intent: Machine record, 250+ words: the corporate template authorizing wake/sleep decisions for terraform seeds — with MOTHER's handwritten-in-script note: 'this one is yours now'.

items.title: Service Record: One (1) Second-Hand Hover-Bike
items.intent: Log, 250+ words: the Wren's maintenance history — three owners, notable dents, one entry in Ketch's handwriting that just says 'good bike, don't tell her'.

items.title: On Walls of Sand: A Meteorology of the Glass Desert
items.intent: Field-guide, 250+ words: how the storms form off windspine, storm-static physics, why radios sing, and the twelve-minute rule.

items.title: Moorage Pay: Collected Stories
items.intent: Log, 250+ words: stories the moorage crew pays water debts with — docked ghosts, a race with the wind, the mailbag that sang.

items.title: Keel Town Hang-Tenants' Agreement
items.intent: Tract, 250+ words: the charter of the town hung off the skydocks rim — weight limits, envy clauses, and the annual 'swing festival'.

items.title: Driftline Application: A. Varga
items.intent: Record, 250+ words: Ash's own courier application — half-qualified, fully stubborn, annotated by Ketch ('teachable') and Tamsin ('insurable, barely').

items.title: Hover Playground
items.intent: A no-stakes hover-bike physics sandbox on a small bespoke dunes map (not the main world): adjustable hover spring, grip, boost, drift parameters via live sliders so players can literally tune the bike. Product: param play toy for tuning feel between releases. Art direction: lab-clean variant of the salt palette — flattened salt pan, teal grid horizon markers, amber parameter chips. Interactions: WASD/Shift/Space driving, sliders update physics same-frame, reset-to-spawn button, parameter presets (arcade/sim/drift missile). Stack: React + R3F; keep self-contained in src/lab/hover-playground/.

items.title: Canyon Slalom Time Trial
items.intent: A standalone 45-second time-trial down a tight procedural glass canyon with checkpoint gates and slick grip, local best time in localStorage. Teaches drifting on glass. Art: teal glass walls, amber gates, dusk light. Interactions: drive, gates split-time deltas rendered in HUD, three retry prompts. Stack: R3F + small analytic heightfield; no missions.

items.title: Skybox & Day Cycle Tuner
items.intent: Design tool: scrub the day/night cycle across the DRIFTLINE palette keyframes (dawn/day/dusk/night) over a bare dune vista, with sliders for fog density, sun intensity, star factor. Exports current settings as JSON to clipboard. Art: cleansing palette, big sky. Stack: R3F + leva-less hand-rolled slider panel.

items.title: Dust & Particle Lab
items.intent: Particle sandbox: tune the driftline dust trail (count, size, lifetime, turbulence, surface colours salt/sand/glass) live while a ghost bike auto-laps a test circuit. Purpose: dial in the game's recycled Points emitters. Art: flat test pan, colour-coded particle systems. Stack: R3F, buffer recycling demo.

items.title: Radio Static Visualizer
items.intent: Audio-reactive art toy: procedural WebAudio noise tuned through 'stations' (Choir static, Guild dispatch beeps, storm band, MOTHER's sleep-breath), driving a cathode-ray-style line scope. Choir-teal scope glow on ink background. Interactions: dial the frequency, hold to 'listen', occasional ghost-harmonics. Stack: Web Audio + canvas 2D.

items.title: Heightfield Explorer
items.intent: Fly-through of the world heightfield in false colour (height bands, surface-kind tint, region masks overlaid) with toggles for each terrain feature (canyon carve, ridge, mesa, flats). Purpose: worldgen debugging and pretty. Interactions: orbit/fly camera, layer toggles, seed display. Stack: R3F + the real lib/terrain module.

items.title: Compass & Minimap Lab
items.intent: UI lab for the HUD navigation: a fake world with draggable anchors to test compass tick positioning, waypoint diamond clamping, minimap contrast at 4 palettes (day/naught no— day/dusk/night/storm). Purpose: prove colour-blind-safe shapes. Stack: pure React + canvas 2D.

items.title: Boost Feedback Lab
items.intent: Feel-lab for boost juice: synthetic bike telemetry drives candidate boost feedbacks (FOV curves, screen shake amps, engine pitch curves, boost-bar drain styles) side by side. Interactions: hold-to-boost on a straight track, A/B toggles. Stack: R3F minimal + HUD prototypes.

items.title: Storm Front Sandbox
items.intent: A wall-of-sand simulator: rolling storm front as curved fog wall + particle sheet crossing a flat pan; sliders for speed, density, turbulence, wall height; try outrunning it on a simple bike. Purpose: tune ch3/ch5 storm missions. Art: ochre wall over violet dusk. Stack: R3F, custom fog shader-lite via FogExp2 modulation + Points.

items.title: Portrait Booth
items.intent: Contact-sheet viewer for all generated character portraits: grid, individual lightbox with the character's voice notes, faction colour framing, and a 'generate prompt' preview of the appearance text (to re-roll art later). Stack: React only, images via withBase.

items.title: Codex Reader Lab
items.intent: Typography playground for the codex: reads lore markdown live from src/content/lore, with toggles for measure, leading, size, and a 'printed Guild form' decorative mode. Purpose: keep 120+ in-world entries genuinely pleasant to read. Stack: React + the codex library.

items.title: Waypoint & Beacon Bench
items.intent: Bench-test mission markers: beam/diamond/ring/collect items/race gates cycling through shapes, colourways and distances on a night-time test range, with colour-blind simulation filters (protan/deutan/tritan) to verify shape-not-colour rule. Stack: R3F + CSS filters.

items.title: Brinn
items.intent: Reclaimer trader camped at Saltmouth's east gate (introduced in ch1-debt-shield). Rust colours, big laugh, honest-ish scales, perpetually selling 'slightly warm' horizon cells. Recurring side-job flavor and reclaimer rep voice in the hub.

items.title: Dockmaster Vane
items.intent: Dockmaster of Keel Town at the skydocks mesa — the Guild's sky port. Runs moorings like a lighthouse keeper who learned accounting. Recipient of ch2-guild-offer custody papers. Voice: airy, clipped, mildly afraid of the ground.

items.title: Old Ferro
items.intent: Ancient moorage hand at the Saltmouth mast; has opinionated friendships with every rope. Pays the player to misfile his eviction notice in side-long-way-home. Warm, rambling, secretly sharp.

items.title: Keeper Solei
items.intent: Keeper of the mid-span shrine on the Glassroad canyon — a truck-stop chapel for couriers. Orders BOOKS (side-canyon-post). Speaks in weathered proverbs and brews terrible tea loved by all.

items.title: TALLY-9 (Substation Caretaker)
items.intent: The drowned-array substation's automated caretaker, awake 200 years past the end of its funding. Still answers mail (side-pan-letters, side-theo-messages). Polite, literal, heartbreakingly cheerful. Lines read like service tickets written by a ghost with good manners.

items.title: Gauge-Keeper Dax
items.intent: Chief of the windspine storm-gauge crew; only opens the hatch at night (side-night-supply). Reads pressure charts like tea leaves, distrusts anyone who hasn't been lied to by a barometer. Dry as the flats.

items.title: Verger Sann
items.intent: Choirmaster-practical: quartermaster of choirhollow who orders the lamp oil and sweeps the crater rim. Grounded counterweight to Ilex's mysticism. Voice: wry, logistical, low-key devout.

items.title: Ratchet June
items.intent: Reclaimer long-haul driver; her crawler 'Second Mortgage' features in ch3-salvage-rights. Radio voice: sings to the engine, swears at the weather, tender with machines.

items.title: Mose Adler
items.intent: Keeper of Saltmouth's water tower; counts cups, blesses pumps, rigs the laundry line couriers keep nearly dying on. Recipient of ch1-watering coil. Voice: slow, grateful, faintly tyrannical about cups.

items.title: Espendez 'Spence' Sorrel
items.intent: Semi-retired Driftline veteran who rode with Ketch in the storm years; now races for fun (side-following-wind flavor). Voice: stories that start 'this one time the sky fell sideways'. A living bit of Driftline history for radio chatter.

items.title: Mallow
items.intent: A Saltmouth kid who times the couriers with a broken stopwatch and reports their laps with brutal honesty. Tutorial-adjacent comic relief; unlocks codex gossip. Independent.

items.title: Clerk Impa Vell
items.intent: Junior Guild clerk at the exchange; idolizes couriers, files everything, including feelings. Voice: over-correct, earnest, asterisks in spoken form. Source of minor guild jobs and ledger gossip.

items.title: Nyx Ala
items.intent: Independent surveyor camped on windspine mapping dune migration; sells waypoint gossip. Voice: precise cartographer poetry, annoyed the desert keeps moving.

items.title: Prior Chance
items.intent: Choir relic-keeper who watches the mothersgate approach from a hermitage; knows the Door's inscription by heart and not what it means. Appears ch4. Voice: half sentences, long brave silences.

items.title: Advocate Reyes
items.intent: Guild advocate in Keel Town who technically owns Ash's debt and sends beautifully worded dunning letters. Not villainous; genuinely thinks the debt gives Ash structure. Comic antagonist energy, ch5 ballot beat.

items.title: Sable
items.intent: A courier who rides only at night ('the day shift has enough of you people'). Mysterious-ish, actually just likes the stars and the cold. Radio chatter voice for night driving; driftline.

items.title: A Primer on the Sleeping Gardener (Choirmaster's edition, annotated)
items.intent: Category: record. A Choir primer on MOTHER: what she is (terraforming intelligence), what the Choir believes (sleeping gardener), glossary of litanies. Needed as reward for ch2-first-word (lore:mother-primer). In-world pamphlet voice, annotated by a sceptical reader.

items.title: Transcript: First Ful Sentences at the Door
items.intent: Category: record. Transcript of MOTHER's first complete sentences at the Door, with timecodes and the transcriber's increasingly unsteady marginalia. Needed as reward for ch4-door-opens (lore:mother-voice). Kind and strange, never menacing.

items.title: Kessa-9 Terraforming Progress Report, Quarter Abandoned
items.intent: Category: record. The official terraforming progress report that was being written when the money ran out — optimistic quarterly language colliding with 'funding suspended' stamps. Explains why Kessa-9 is half a garden.

items.title: Incident Rept 7-K: The Burn That Made the Road
items.intent: Category: record. Incident report on the reactor burn that fused the Glassroad canyon to teal glass. Written by an engineer who stayed. Explains why the glass is fast, slick, and faintly warm.

items.title: Turbine 9 Maintenance Log (storm season entries)
items.intent: Category: log. A windspine turbine keeper's maintenance log across one storm season: bird nests, vows to quit, aurora nights, the season's first wall of sand. Foreshadows ch3.

items.title: Keel Town Mooring Tariffs (posted, amended, argued)
items.intent: Category: tract. Keel Town mooring tariff poster with two centuries of handwritten amendments, feuds in the margins, and one fee listed only as 'don't ask'. Skydocks flavor.

items.title: Yard Rules, The (Reclaimer Union, local 3)
items.intent: Category: tract. The Reclaimer yard rules of cinderflats: what you may strip, what you may not (list short), how to address Aunt Vertex's charges, funeral etiquette for machines.

items.title: Listening Rota, Hollow of the First Note
items.intent: Category: log. Choirhollow's listening schedule: who sits at which horn at which hour, what they've heard, and the column where Little Reverb's notes keep being right.

items.title: Substation Caretaker Log, years 1 through 203
items.intent: Category: log. TALLY-9's substation log: 200 years of 'all systems nominal' degrading into 'all systems absent, spirits high'. Melancholy centerpiece for drowned-array.

items.title: Final Survey, Terraform Cradle Approach (sealed)
items.intent: Category: record. The last survey of mothersgate before it was sealed shut: elevations, anomalous readings, and the surveyor's recommendation: 'seal it, bill it, forget it' (two of three completed).

items.title: The Courier's Storm Almanac, 44th edition
items.intent: Category: field-guide. A courier's almanac of storm season: wall types, shelter etiquette, what to do if the wind starts singing (it isn't; if it is, that's the Choir's problem).

items.title: Ketch's Maintenance Wall: Notes for New Idiots
items.intent: Category: field-guide. Ketch's hover-bike maintenance notes, in his hand: hover spring damping, gyro rings, why the Wren pulls left ('character'). Practical and fond.

items.title: Horizon Cell Care: A Field Pamphlet (Salt Guild Press)
items.intent: Category: field-guide. Horizon cell care and feeding: charge cycles, heat warnings, a stern paragraph on buying 'slightly warm' cells from traders (see: incidents, fire, Brinn).

items.title: Stories Swapped at Relay Fires (collected)
items.intent: Category: tract. Driftline ghost stories swapped at relay fires: the Pale Courier, the crate that delivers itself, the beacon that answers. Each story annotated 'true' by someone reliable and 'nonsense' by Ketch.

items.title: Audit Memos, Office of the Counterweight
items.intent: Category: record. A run of Sister Counterweight's audit memos: calibration procedures, the soul-weighing protocol (standard practice), and the one memo shorter than all the others, about the crate.

items.title: Kessa-9 Frequency Map (unofficial, tattooed on a courier's arm)
items.intent: Category: field-guide. Who talks on which channel: Guild dispatch, Driftline chatter, Choir listening bands, Reclaimer work channels, and the frequency nobody admits to using since the crate.

items.title: Night Market Menu Broadcast, Keel Town (with prices)
items.intent: Category: broadcast. Keel Town night-market radio menu read-aloud: spice prices, noodle stall feuds, weather disclaimers courtesy of the goat. Warm slice-of-life.

items.title: Air Check: An Interview with Jett Marrows
items.intent: Category: broadcast. A sports-radio interview with Jett Marrows: training regime ('winning'), feelings about the new courier ('who?'), gate ethics ('optimistic').

items.title: Manifest and Route: Davenant, R. (final run)
items.intent: Category: record. Rill Davenant's manifest and route slips from the run he didn't come back from. Everything ordinary, one gap. ch3 foreshadow; should send a chill.

items.title: Three Static Litanies, with Translations
items.intent: Category: tract. Excerpts from the Choir's static litanies with translations from the hiss; gentle, strange, occasionally too accurate about tomorrow.

items.title: The Salvage Code (annotated by three feuding editors)
items.intent: Category: tract. The Reclaimer salvage code: first-touch law, hazard shares, what counts as 'abandoned' (definition 4 pages long; item: doors). Underpins ch3-salvage-rights.

items.title: Saltmouth Water Charter (hydration provisions, amended)
items.intent: Category: record. Saltmouth's water charter: who owns rain, cups, towers, and the concept of thirst. The bit where the Guild graciously permits hydration, cited in ch1-watering.

items.title: Methods of the Guild Weather Desk (caprine division)
items.intent: Category: field-guide. The Guild weather desk's methodology: one goat, three clerks, prediction accuracy statistics the clerks are afraid to publish. Pemmy's greatest forecasts.

items.title: Notes on Riding Glass (learned the fast way)
items.intent: Category: field-guide. Why canyon glass is fast: structure, heat, grip, the smugness problem. A courier's physics for people who learn by crashing.

items.title: Working Notes: On Opening What Should Stay Shut
items.intent: Category: record. Reclaimer engineering speculation on the null crate as a wake-key: three disassembly quotes, one casserole recipe, and a warning in Boss Pyke's hand: 'not yet'.

items.title: A Short History of Holding the Line
items.intent: Category: tract. A short history of the courier oath: who wrote it (disputed), who broke it (list), who died keeping it (longer list, honoured).

items.title: Beacon Tender's Manual, Glass Desert Loop
items.intent: Category: field-guide. Road beacons of the Driftline: spacing, relighting, why beacon 41 is haunted (it is not; it is lonely). Companion to side-beacon-sweep.

items.title: Storm Shelters of the Glass Desert: Critical Notices
items.intent: Category: field-guide. Storm shelter locations and reviews, by couriers: star ratings given in 'minutes of life saved', one shelter reviewed only 'has a dog'.

items.title: Dock Shanties of Keel Town (field transcriptions)
items.intent: Category: tract. Dock shanties of Keel Town, transcribed: hauling songs, mooring songs, the one about the ground ('soft, no rigging, distrusted').

items.title: Weighing Log (salt and otherwise), excerpts
items.intent: Category: record. Sister Counterweight's soul-and-salt weighing log: procedure, results, one entry left blank except for a scale reading and a request for transfer.

items.title: The Keepers of the Door: A Garage Lineage
items.intent: Category: log. The line of Saltmouth garage keepers, two centuries of names painted over the door, with what each added to the creed wall.

items.title: The Words Above the Door (copy, worn)
items.intent: Category: record. The inscription over the cradle door at mothersgate, as copied by Prior Chance: text, wear patterns, and her notes on which letters she dreams about.

items.title: Transcripts of the Emergency Manifest Hearings
items.intent: Category: record. Guild hearing transcripts about the humming crate: testimony from the night dog, a ruling that philosophy is uninsurable, adjournment due to humming.

items.title: What If It Rained: A Modest Enquiry
items.intent: Category: broadcast. A Keel Town think-piece: what if it rained? Economics, theology, poetry. Both endings quietly foreshadowed; wistful, hopeful.

items.title: A Childhood Field Guide to Salt Blooms
items.intent: Category: field-guide. Salt-bloom ecology of the flats: crystal gardens, what eats them (nothing), why couriers name the pretty ones.

items.title: The Ballad of the Wren (radio play transcript)
items.intent: Category: broadcast. A courier radio play aired for new riders: the ballad of the Wren (the player's bike, before it was the player's). Ketch cameos. Heartbreaker, funny.

items.title: The Last Wire: How the Money Ran Out
items.intent: Category: record. Why the money ran out: terraforming economics, the last budget hearing on Earth feed-lag, the final wire transfer annotation ('sorry').

items.title: Visitor's Book, Mid-Span Chapel
items.intent: Category: log. Dedication plaque and visitor's book of the mid-span glass chapel: 200 years of couriers signing in, one entry per storm survived.

items.title: Found Static: The Lullaby on the Dead Channel
items.intent: Category: broadcast. Found static: an old terraforming-era lullaby broadcast that loops on a dead channel; the Choir leaves it playing;歌词 unknown, everyone hums along. Wait — no Chinese. Lyrics unknown, everyone hums along.

items.title: Night Lines: A Dark-Hours Riding Guide
items.intent: Category: field-guide. Riding in the dark: night routes, star navigation, who else rides at night (Sable), and why the desert is honest after sunset.

items.title: Ferro's Rope Tally (with commentary)
items.intent: Category: log. Moorage Old Ferro's rope tally: every ship he's moored, every storm he's watched, the knot he invented and named after someone he doesn't discuss.

items.title: Project Kessa-9: Pause Memo (unaudited)
items.intent: The old planetcrack memo that ended everything: HelioDyne's cost-analysis declaring Kessa-9 41% terraformed and 0% profitable. Cold corporate voice, the money running out in a spreadsheet.

items.title: MAINTENANCE LOG, cycle 74412 (excerpt)
items.intent: MOTHER's dormant state from the inside: a boot-log fragment cycling self-checks for two centuries, timestamps drifting, one line repeating with growing variation. Category: record.

items.title: Last Day at the Array (dawn re-broadcast #72,923)
items.intent: What the Drowned Array's caretaker machine remembers: a broadcast it recorded the day the crews left, replayed to nobody every dawn for 200 years. Category: broadcast.

items.title: Glass Blooms: First Observations
items.intent: Field guide entry: glass blooms — the new crystal flowers erupting along the Glassroad in ch4. Observation notes, sketches-in-words, warnings. Category: field-guide.

items.title: The Doctrine of the Cradle (visitor's edition)
items.intent: Choir tract: the doctrine of the Cradle — where MOTHER sleeps, why the Choir carries light to her, why couriers are honorary clergy on crater roads.

items.title: Storm Gauge Journal, Season Open
items.intent: Windspine weather log, entry style: the storm season building day by day, wind gauge readings climbing, the keeper's notes getting shorter and worse. Category: log.

items.title: Saltmouth Shipping Bulletin, No. 1,204
items.intent: The day's shipping bulletin, miraculous mundanity: flour flats, a lost dog, one anomalous crate with no manifest, and a small flood of 'no further questions' in the margins. Category: broadcast.

items.title: Of the First Brinemaster (approved history)
items.intent: Guild ledgers as scripture: the Guild's own founding story — the first Brinemaster, the first scale, the first lie caught by the second. Category: record.

items.title: Night Riding: A Courier's Notes
items.intent: Field guide: riding at night — violet sky, cold glass, stars, the way the desert reads your headlight and the things that read it back.

items.title: The Salt Harvest and Its Enemies
items.intent: A tract by the salt-farmers on the flats' edge: the glass harvest, what fused silica tastes like, trade with the Guild on terms of proud mutual resentment.

items.title: Keel Town Docking Gazette (weekly)
items.intent: Keel Town's own paper: a skyship docking schedule laced with gossip — who shipped what, who isn't talking, one entry that just says 'the crate passed by again'. Category: record.

items.title: Eleven Minutes: the Reactor Seven Burn
items.intent: History: how the fused-glass canyon formed in eleven minutes when Reactor Seven burned, and why the floor sings at night. Category: record.

items.title: Services for the Retired Machine (Local 9 liturgy)
items.intent: Reclaimer liturgy for machinery: Aunt Vertex's full service for retiring a machine — said over turbines, haulers, and once a vending unit. Category: tract.

items.title: Turbine Row Survey, Week of the Ninth
items.intent: Turbine survey notes: nesting birds, stolen bolts, a Choir pilgrim camped on a pylon, readings wrong in a way that *predicts* storms. Category: log.

items.title: Entries Removed From the Master Ledger (index of)
items.intent: What has been politely scratched out of the master ledgers over the years — a catalogue of redactions, each scratched line more interesting than the entry it ruined. Category: record.

items.title: Lamp Rest Night Broadcast (transcript)
items.intent: The Choir's midnight playlist, verbatim: hours of static, one record cough every forty minutes, the congregation breathing on mic, love at 2 a.m. Category: broadcast.

items.title: The Lost Couriers Archive
items.intent: Every Driftline rider who didn't come home: name, bike, last route, last radio word. Maintained by Ketch. The most sacred non-religious document on the salt. Category: record.

items.title: On the Fair and Holy Price of Water
items.intent: Guild water pricing, explained: condenser math, tower fees, the sun tax that nobody calls a sun tax, why Pemmy the goat has a signature line. Category: tract.

items.title: Cradle Door, Systems Report (auto-generated)
items.intent: First contact with mothersgate in ch4: the door's health report after 200 years — all systems green, one small anomaly (a printer that should have no power). Category: record.

items.title: Courier Log of R. Davenant (final run)
items.intent: Rill Davenant's log, mid-vanishing: entries drifting from competent to coordinate-mad, weather notes becoming liturgy. Category: log.

items.title: Riding the Wall: A Storm Guide
items.intent: Field guide to storm-chasing for couriers: riding the wall's lee, reading gust color, when to race a front and when to let it baptise you.

items.title: Strip Me Gently: Collected Odes
items.intent: Poems to stripped machinery by Mags Delver, hauler: odes to a cooling tower, elegy for a conveyor, one haiku about a bolt she 'shouldn't have loved'. Category: tract.

items.title: Moorage Master Log (200 years, condensed)
items.intent: Old lighter-than-air anchorage logs from before the money ran out: skyships that never came back, a fleet list with one ship marginally noted 'late'. Category: log.

items.title: LOCAL NOTICE: Resumption of Services
items.intent: MOTHER's first local notice after waking, broadcast to every speaker on Kessa-9: irrigation schedules resuming, soil apologies, a question about whether anyone missed the rain. Category: broadcast.

items.title: The Storm Gauge Keeper's Log
items.intent: Log excerpts from the windspine storm-gauge keeper across one storm season; meter readings that don't match the calendar, a wall that arrived a day early, and the unsettling entry where the barometer 'answered back'.

items.title: Toll Songs of the Glass Road
items.intent: Collected road-songs couriers sing to time their canyon braking points; each verse encodes a real hazard on the glassroad, with a note from a Guild folklorist who tried to tax the singing itself.

items.title: Fragment: MOTHER Maintenance Manifest, Cycle 0x2F
items.intent: A machine record from the last days of full terraforming: seed dispersal schedules, aerosol budgets, one line of maternal affection smuggled into a checksum field. Ends abruptly mid-line.

items.title: Grace Before Salvage: Reclaimer Meal Prayers
items.intent: The short prayers reclaimer crews say before cutting into old infrastructure — equal parts apology to the machine, insurance against ghosts, and practical blame-assignment for whoever holds the torch.

items.title: Three Static Litanies (Annotated)
items.intent: Three canonical Choir 'static litanies' — prayers spoken into dead radios — with margin notes by a younger initiate who keeps hearing actual words in the noise and is afraid to say so.

items.title: Extract from the Great Ledger of Debts, Saltmouth Column
items.intent: A page from the Guild's debt ledger: names, sums, odd collateral ('one (1) affectionate goat'), margin doodles, and a fresh entry stamped in a hand nobody at the exchange admits to using: A. VARGA.

items.title: Census of the Drowned Array
items.intent: A field guide to the submerged solar array: which panels still trickle charge, where the cache cairns sit, what sings under the salt pan at night, and the surveyor who's named every panel and mourns the sunken ones.

items.title: Keel Town Moorage Rules, Seventh Revision
items.intent: The skydocks' moorage regulations — windshear etiquette, ballast taxes, the famous Balloon Incident clause — annotated by a dockmaster with strong opinions and weak hemispheres of patience.

items.title: The Crusher: Operator's Manual (Abridged, Annotated)
items.intent: Boss Pyke's abridged manual for the big crusher at the yards: safety margins redacted for speed, Aunt Vertex's explosive addenda, and the list of things that are, formally, 'not for crushing'.

items.title: Rill Davenant's Marginal Route Notes
items.intent: Recovered notes from the courier who goes missing in storm season: scrawled bearings, weather hunches, and an increasingly worried running joke about a voice that knows their name.

items.title: The Printer That Shouldn't Have Power: A Print Log
items.intent: A Guild auditor investigates how the null crate was printed on a machine without power for a century: toner assays, impossible timestamps, and the auditor's growing professional horror.

items.title: The Horizon Cell Handbook for Depressed Couriers
items.intent: A cheerfully cynical zine about bike batteries: charging etiquette, cold-weather sulking, why your horizon cell hates you, and one page that is just a poem to lithium.

items.title: Two Maps, One Lie: Kessa-9 Before and During
items.intent: An annotated comparison of the terraforming prospectus map (verdant, generous) and a surveyor's honest chart two centuries later; the narrator's fondness for the real one is unmistakable.

items.title: On the Chemistry and Politics of Manifest Wax
items.intent: Why Guild seals matter: the wax recipe, the colour grades that encode cargo class, the scandal of the counterfeit teal seal, and why breaking a seal wrong can legally unmarry someone.

items.title: Lamp-lighting Rounds of the Hollow
items.intent: A day in choirhollow told through the lamp-lighting rounds: who carries which ladder, which lamp is 'the difficult one', and what the crater does to voices after dusk.

items.title: A Working Lexicon of Driftline Slang
items.intent: Forty-odd terms couriers actually use: 'glassed', 'dusted', 'wax-blind', 'a Ketch', 'riding the hum' — with etymologies, disdainful corrections, and entries clearly written to insult specific people.

items.title: Survey 1902: The Sealed Cradle
items.intent: The last pre-dormancy survey of mothersgate: measurements of the Door, seismic notes, the surveyor's insistence that the mechanism 'listened', and the order to bury the report.

items.title: Night Riding: A Primer for the Reasonably Brave
items.intent: How to ride the glass desert after dark: violet light, cold-snap handling, which lights to trust (teal), which to avoid (amber that moves wrong), and the etiquette of night beacons.

items.title: Transcript: An Interview with the Quicklime Kid
items.intent: A zine journalist interviews the region's most annoying prodigy rider mid-ride: philosophy of marker-shaving, diet of warm soda, and one chillingly competent paragraph about drift lines.

items.title: After-Action: The Wall That Took Bitter Flats
items.intent: The Guild's after-action report on the legendary storm that erased a settlement in one night: what failed, who stayed, and the rider who carried forty-two people out in a cargo wagon.

items.title: The Season's First Wall (ch3 storm run)
items.intent: Storm-season story beat: routes closing; Ketch sends Ash on the first true wall-run of the year — outrun a season-opening storm front from the glassroad south gate to temple-step shelter; teaches the 'storm' objective in-story (side-storm-window is the tutorial side version).

items.title: The Cache Cairn Round
items.intent: Collect-type side job in the drowned array: haul out five sealed pre-collapse cache canisters from around the cache cairn and panel field before the pan's night-sink makes the footing treacherous.

items.title: Ladder and Lamp
items.intent: Escort-type Choir side job in choirhollow: shadow the slow lamp-lighters' wagon around the lamp ring at dusk; the Choir pays in lamp oil futures and unsettlingly specific blessings.

items.title: Dockmaster's Express
items.intent: Timed delivery between skydocks anchors: ballast affidavits from winch base up to Keel Town before the evening updraft window closes; tight timer, high-altitude riding, dockmaster barks.

items.title: Parts for the Crusher
items.intent: Fragile-type reclaimer side job: carry a gyro-stabilised cutting head from Pyke's office to the crusher without cracking its ceramic collar — the yards are full of things to bump into, which is the joke and the hazard.

items.title: The Mesa Survey
items.intent: Scout-type side job across three viewpoint anchors (dune overlook, ridge crest, crater rim): hold position at each for the Guild's new cartography contract; pays better the less your bike complains.

items.title: Rematch on the Slick Mile
items.intent: Race-type side job vs. Jett Marrows down the glassroad slick mile at dusk: five gates, glass-slick grip, rival trash-talk on the radio, and a purse paid in genuine antique bottle caps (convertible).

items.title: The Missing Mail Satchel
items.intent: Chase-type side job: a courier's mail satchel was snatched by a joyriding dock-brat on a stolen skiff around the saltmouth pan; run them down, tag them, get the satchel back before the stamps absorb moisture and become legally soup.

items.title: Dialogue Stage — portrait & line-set preview bench
items.intent: A dialogue-scene staging bench for DRIFTLINE writers and designers: pick any two characters (from src/content/characters), a backdrop region (day/dusk/night sky variations), and preview their portraits, voice-notes and sample lines rendered in the real DialogueBox layout at multiple screen sizes. Features: line editor with live preview, timing playback (auto-advance at reading speed), choice-tree mock mode with flag chips, export of a dialogue JSON block ready to paste into a mission file. Art direction: frontier-western solarpunk, sun-bleached salt/ochre/teal palette per DESIGN.md, Chakra Petch display + Sora body fonts, violet-dark sheet UI. Audience: DRIFTLINE content writers and the builder verifying dialogue feel without booting the full game. Stack: React + DOM overlay components reusing src/ui/ui.css; load characters via the same dialogue library glob.

items.title: Storm Choreo — storm-wall pursuit tuning sim
items.intent: A storm-wall choreography simulator: stage the DRIFTLINE storm objective on a scrolling top-down tactical view — move the shelter anchor, storm spawn offset, storm speed curve and radius with sliders, then watch a simulated courier (straight-line with reaction noise) attempt the run and see survival probability over N Monte Carlo trials flip live. Purpose: tune storm missions so they're tense but fair before writers ship them. Features: minimap-style canvas view in the game's danger-red/amber palette, tuneable pursuit curve, difficulty readout, export mission objective JSON. Art direction: DRIFTLINE HUD language — violet-dark panels, amber markers, danger-red storm wedge, tabular numerals, Chakra Petch. Audience: mission designers and the builder. Stack: React + canvas2d, no 3D needed; constants mirror src/game/MissionDirector storm params.

items.title: Traffic Planner — ambient loop route editor
items.intent: An ambient-traffic planner for the open world: a top-down map of Kessa-9 showing all region circles and named anchors, where you draw/edit NPC loop routes (courier, hauler, skiff classes with speed/colour presets) and replay miniature dots cruising them to judge congestion and dead zones. One click exports the route arrays in the exact VehicleSpec format used by src/game/AmbientTraffic.tsx. Features: anchor snapping, route length + lap-time readout, per-class silhouette preview dot, random auto-generated routes. Art direction: in-world surveyor's table look — bone paper texture tint (flat), rust ruled lines, teal glass accents, hand-stamped labels, entirely CSS/canvas2d. Audience: the builder and demo builders extending world life. Stack: React + canvas2d; reads region registry data statically.
